s: Alice Waters' 1971 Shattuck Avenue house that invented California cuisine, still serving a nightly fixed-price menu downstairs.
w: Alice Waters opened Chez Panisse in a converted Berkeley bungalow in 1971, and the prix-fixe downstairs restaurant still changes its single nightly menu with the Bay Area's harvests, exactly as it did when the idea of 'farm to table' didn't have a name yet. Upstairs, the more casual Café keeps its own à la carte menu and wood-fired oven running.
_facts: Widely credited with founding California cuisine

s: A Fillmore Street dining room where dim-sum-style carts circle the tables loaded with California small plates instead of dumplings.
w: Stuart Brioza and Nicole Krasinski built State Bird Provisions around a gimmick that outlasted the gimmick stage: servers wheel carts and trays past every table, and diners flag down whatever small plate looks good, from the namesake stuffed quail to changing vegetable dishes. Michelin star since it opened in 2011.
_facts: Opened 2011 by chefs Stuart Brioza and Nicole Krasinski
Known for the signature fried quail

s: A cavernous Mission District bakery-restaurant-bar where Tartine's sourdough turns up in wood-fired pizza as often as in a loaf.
w: Bakers Chad Robertson and Elisabeth Prueitt expanded their Tartine name into this warehouse-scale Alabama Street space, running a bakery counter, coffee bar, full restaurant, and bar out of one long room. Dinner leans on sourdough-crust pizza and a market-driven menu alongside a global wine list.
_facts: Founded by Chad Robertson and Elisabeth Prueitt
Combines bakery, coffee bar, restaurant, and bar

s: A husband-and-wife-run New American spot near Hayes Valley known for foraged, playful plates like its long-running porcini doughnut.
w: Chefs Evan and Sarah Rich opened Rich Table in 2012 in a plain storefront near Gough and Oak, building a menu around forage-driven, technique-heavy plates -- the porcini doughnut with raclette fondue has stayed on the menu for over a decade. Spun off RT Rotisserie and RT Bistro nearby.
_facts: Opened 2012 by chefs Evan and Sarah Rich

s: Chef Pim Techamuanvivit's contemporary Thai dining room set inside the Hotel Kabuki in Japantown.
w: Pim Techamuanvivit, who also runs Kin Khao in SF and Nahm in Bangkok, opened Nari inside the Hotel Kabuki in 2019, filtering Thai cooking through California produce and her own Bangkok upbringing. Holds a Michelin star.

s: A restored century-old apothecary building in the Outer Richmond turned into a handmade-pasta dining room and cocktail bar.
w: Pearl 6101 occupies a converted turn-of-the-century pharmacy on California Street, its narrow dining room and full bar built into the original shopfront bones. The kitchen runs a California-meets-Mediterranean menu of handmade pastas, whole fish, and family-style meats.
_facts: Housed in a restored early-1900s apothecary building
Handmade pastas, whole fish, family-style meats

s: A Hayes Valley bakery-café in the old 20th Century Café space, built around Jewish and Levantine diaspora pastry.
w: Loquat opened on Gough Street, co-owned by Tal Mor (also a partner in Four Barrel Coffee/the Mill) and Jodi Geren, with pastry chef Kristina Costa -- formerly of Tartine -- leading the kitchen. The case runs on babka, bourekas, and other pastries drawn from across the Jewish diaspora.
_facts: Co-owned by Tal Mor and Jodi Geren

s: A Lower Haight storefront turning out sourdough-crust pizza that built its following through pop-ups before landing a permanent home.
w: Jules built a cult reservation list as a pop-up before opening this brick-and-mortar on Fillmore Street, carrying its sourdough pizza program into a proper kitchen. The room is small and the menu tight, weighted toward the pies that made the pop-up's name.
_facts: Began as a pop-up before opening this permanent location

s: A Mission District wine-forward dining room pairing Californian-Mediterranean cooking with a deep, unusual list.
w: Heirloom Cafe occupies a corner storefront on Folsom Street in the Mission, built around cooking that leans Californian with Mediterranean and French touches. The wine list is the real draw for regulars -- deep, idiosyncratic, and assembled with more curiosity than most restaurants twice its size attempt.
_facts: Californian-Mediterranean menu with French technique influence
Known for an extensive, eclectic wine list

s: A Mission District Italian restaurant that helped set off San Francisco's modern handmade-pasta wave.
w: Flour + Water opened in 2009 on Harrison Street and became a template for a generation of SF pasta restaurants that followed, pairing a constantly rotating handmade-pasta list with wood-fired Neapolitan pizza. Still a same-day-line kind of restaurant for walk-ins.
_facts: Known for handmade pasta and Neapolitan-style pizza

s: A rustic Italian trattoria in Jackson Square, the casual sibling to Quince next door, built around a wood-fired oven.
w: Chef Michael Tusk runs Cotogna as the more casual, lower-priced counterpart to his Michelin-starred Quince, sharing a building at the corner of Montgomery and Pacific. The open kitchen's wood-fired oven turns out pizzas and roasted meats alongside daily house-made pasta.

s: A Lower Haight wine bar that plays down its ambitions, built around chef Robert Hernandez's small-plates cooking and a deep natural wine list.
w: Bar Jabroni bills itself as a neighborhood wine bar, but chef Robert Hernandez's kitchen runs a genuine small-plates program behind that modest framing, built on French-gastropub instincts and seasonal ingredients. The natural wine list is long and changes often.

s: Thomas Keller's stone farmhouse in Yountville, three Michelin stars since the guide first rated California, and still one of the hardest reservations in America.
w: Thomas Keller took over a 19th-century stone building that once housed a literal French steam laundry and turned it, in 1994, into the restaurant that reset American fine dining's ambitions. Reservations open exactly one month ahead and the wait list forms within minutes; Keller's culinary garden sits directly across Washington Street.
_facts: Culinary garden sits across the street

s: An Outer Sunset corner wine shop and sandwich counter serving arm-length hoagies alongside natural wine to drink in or take home.
w: Palm City occupies a corner storefront on Irving Street in the Outer Sunset, running as a natural wine shop, bar, and sandwich counter at once -- a hoagie stretched the length of your forearm, plus a chopped salad, paired with a bottle off the shop shelves. Built for lingering rather than turning tables.
_facts: Combines a wine shop, bar, and sandwich counter

s: A tasting menu ordered off a laminated card of emoji, no dish names attached, served in a converted Sukhumvit townhouse.
w: Gaggan Anand closed his original Soi Langsuan restaurant at the top of its game in 2019 and rebuilt under his own name a short walk from Sukhumvit Soi 31. The menu is still a strip of icons, decoded only when the plate lands. Indian technique runs underneath modern plating.
_facts: Chef Gaggan Anand, trained under Ferran Adrià at El Bulli
Menu presented as emoji rather than written descriptions

s: Thai-Chinese tasting menu served inside a century-old Sino-Portuguese shophouse that was once the chef's family pharmacy.
w: Chef Pichaya 'Pam' Soontornyanakij built Potong inside the actual building where her grandparents dispensed Chinese medicine on Charoen Krung Road. The tasting menu threads Teochew and Hainanese family cooking through French technique. One Michelin star.
_facts: Housed in a restored Sino-Portuguese building

s: German twin brothers cooking schnitzel-and-offal fine dining in a 1970s Bangkok family house they converted room by room.
w: Thomas and Mathias Sühring turned their own rented villa off Yen Akat Road into a restaurant, keeping the staircases, bedrooms, and garden intact. The cooking is unapologetically German -- pretzel, blood sausage, veal tafelspitz -- remade with two-star French technique.
_facts: Twin chefs Thomas and Mathias Sühring

s: A tasting menu that maps Thailand's seasonal produce region by region, from a chef who traded a New York kitchen for Silom.
w: Chef Thitid 'Ton' Tassanakajohn named the restaurant Le Du after the Thai word for 'season,' and the menu changes to track what's arriving from specific provinces. He trained in New York before returning to Bangkok. Michelin star since the first Bangkok guide.
_facts: Michelin star since the first Bangkok guide

s: A ten-seat dining room named after the chef's grandmother, tucked into Bangkok's old town within sight of Wat Pho.
w: Chef Ton Tassanakajohn opened Nusara as a companion to Le Du, naming it for the grandmother whose cooking first taught him Thai food, seating only ten guests a night in Rattanakosin's old quarter. The twelve-course menu draws on regional family recipes.
_facts: Named after chef Ton Tassanakajohn's grandmother

s: Southern Thai cooking, chilies and all, served in a restored two-story mansion off Sukhumvit Soi 26.
w: Chefs Supaksorn 'Ice' Jongsiri and Yodkwan U-Pumpruk built Sorn around the food of Thailand's deep south -- dishes most Bangkok tasting menus soften because of their heat and funk. In 2024 it became the first restaurant in Thailand to hold three Michelin stars.
_facts: First restaurant in Thailand with three Michelin stars, 2024
Specializes in Southern Thai regional cuisine

s: French cooking on the seventh floor of a Marunouchi office tower, run inside a Four Seasons dining room.
w: Sézanne sits above the ground-floor bustle of Tokyo Station's business district, inside a hotel dining room built into one of Asia's most decorated openings of the 2020s. The cooking is French in structure but leans on Japanese seafood and produce sourced daily. Three Michelin stars; named Asia's Best Restaurant 2023 and 2024.
_facts: 7th floor of the Four Seasons Hotel Tokyo at Marunouchi

s: A satoyama-themed tasting menu built around a table centerpiece of live soil, moss, and yeast starter.
w: Chef Yoshihiro Narisawa calls his cooking 'satoyama' after the Japanese term for land where forest meets farmed field. After a 2023 renovation and a temporary residency in Singapore, it reopened at its original Minami-Aoyama address, a fixture of the World's 50 Best list two decades on.
_facts: Chef Yoshihiro Narisawa coined the 'satoyama cuisine' concept
Reopened at original address after 2023 renovation

a: Azabudai Hills Garden Plaza D, Toranomon
s: Chef Hiroyasu Kawate's French-Japanese tasting counter, now inside the glass-and-garden Azabudai Hills complex.
w: Florilège spent its first decade in a basement room near Gaienmae before chef Hiroyasu Kawate closed that chapter in mid-2023 and reopened three months later inside Azabudai Hills. French technique applied to Japanese vegetables and seafood, plated with an emphasis on texture over decoration.

s: French cooking built from kudzu, yuba, and miso, served in a Kawaramachi dining room chef Yusuke Takada calls 'nouvelle cuisine française'.
w: Yusuke Takada trained in France and Belgium before returning to Osaka to build a menu he insists on calling French rather than fusion, even as it runs on tofu skin, kudzu starch, and regional Japanese vegetables. Two Michelin stars; long-standing spot on Asia's 50 Best.
_facts: Chef Yusuke Takada, trained in France and Belgium

s: Julien Royer's French dining room set inside the colonnaded Supreme Court wing of the National Gallery.
w: Odette occupies a corner of the old Supreme Court building, now the National Gallery, with high colonial ceilings and a floral centerpiece that changes with the season. Chef Julien Royer, from Cantal in France, builds the cooking around ingredients flown in from small producers he names on the menu itself.

s: Vicky Cheng's 'boundary-less' Chinese tasting menu, one floor above his French-Chinese debut restaurant Vea.
w: Vicky Cheng opened Wing after a decade of French-trained cooking at Vea, a floor below in the same Central tower, to work in the Chinese cuisine he'd grown up on. The tasting menu draws on Cantonese, Sichuan, and other regional Chinese traditions. Ranked No. 2 in Asia in 2026.
_facts: Chef-owner Vicky Cheng, also runs Vea one floor below

s: Cantonese cooking built on a relationship with a single named farm, in a dining room hung with local artists' work.
w: The Chairman sources produce, poultry, and rice from specific, named farms across the Pearl River Delta. The menu runs on slow-cooked Cantonese classics -- steamed flowery crab, aged soy chicken. It relocated from Kau U Fong to The Wellington building in 2022 and took the top spot on Asia's 50 Best in 2026.
_facts: Known for direct relationships with named farms

s: Chef Mingoo Kang's Korean tasting menu, doenjang and gochujang reworked with the plating grammar of European fine dining.
w: Mingoo Kang trained in France and Italy before returning to Seoul to build Mingles around Korean pantry staples -- fermented soybean paste, chili paste, aged kimchi -- rather than importing a foreign cuisine wholesale. Three Michelin stars; named Korea's best restaurant on Asia's 50 Best.
_facts: Named top restaurant in South Korea by Asia's 50 Best
